To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

all-nanoelelectronic circuits can operate at high frequencies, but not as fast as the fastest nanodevices, and that the performance of such circuits can be enhanced by the use of novel circuit architectures and by the use of nanoscale devices that are not yet available.

the performance of all-nanodevice clocking circuits is limited primarily by the frequency of the nanodevices, and that the maximum achievable operating frequencies of these nano circuits are in the 1 GHz and ISO MHz range for analog and digital applications, respectively.

the performance of nano circuits is limited by their intrinsic device parameters, and that such circuits, if built with presently available devices, can achieve frequencies up to approximately ISO MHz for digital applications, and up to approximately 1000 MHz for analog applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of nano circuits for nanoscale applications, and with the development of nanodevices for use in such circuits.
the development of nanodevice-based clocking circuits for use in stand-alone nanoelectronic devices, nanoelectronic computer systems, and mixed-signal nanoscale electronic systems.
the design of nanoscale clocking circuits for nanocomputing and other nanosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the performance of all-nanodevice-based clocking circuits, if fabricated using presently available nanofabrication processes, could be comparable to or better than that of the best available silicon circuits, but with the advantage of operating at lower supply voltages.

the results presented here indicate the possibility for the development of nanoelectronic clock generators that could achieve clock frequencies in the range of 10's to 100's MHz for digital nanosystems and 10's to hundreds of MHz for analog nanosystems.

the clocking circuits described here, which are intended for use with presently available nanodevice technologies, are capable of operating at clocking frequencies of up to approximately ISO MHz for digital applications and approximately 1 GHz in the analog realm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that nanoelectronic clock circuits can be designed to meet the performance requirements of a wide variety of nano applications.
we have shown that it is possible to construct clocking nano circuits that can operate in the gigahertz range using presently available nanotechnology.

the performance bounds for the clocking nano circuits that we studied are comparable to the performance limits of presently available nanoelectronic devices, but are still far short of the ultimate performance that might be achieved with future nanodevices.

nanoelectronic circuits can achieve clock frequencies that are competitive with those of microelectronic circuits, but with significantly reduced power consumption.
